name: TCS3200 colour sensor module
description: Colour sensor module built on the ams (TAOS) TCS3200 programmable colour light-to-frequency converter: an 8 x 8 photodiode array (16 red, 16 green, 16 blue, 16 clear) whose selected group drives a square wave on OUT with frequency proportional to irradiance. S2/S3 pick the photodiodes (LL red, LH blue, HL clear, HH green), S0/S1 the output scaling (LL power down, LH 2 %, HL 20 %, HH 100 %; full scale typ. 12 / 120 / 600 kHz), OE (active low) enables OUT. Runs on 2.7-5.5 V, 2 mA for the chip plus the four white illumination LEDs; inputs accept VIH >= 2 V, OUT swings to VCC, so power it from 3.3 V on a 3.3 V board. Sold as: generic TCS3200 / TCS230 colour recognition sensor module (28.4 x 28.4 mm, four white LEDs, two 4-pin headers S0/S1/OE/GND and VCC/OUT/S2/S3), the common clone sold by Robu, HowToMechatronics/RandomNerd tutorials and many hobby shops (the older TCS230 version is pin-compatible).
eli5: A tiny eye with red, green, blue and plain filters: it beeps out a fast click train, and the brighter the chosen colour, the faster it clicks. Counting clicks for each filter tells you what colour is in front of it.

driver.code:
# TCS3200 / TCS230 colour sensor module, MicroPython driver.
# The ams/TAOS TCS3200 is a light-to-frequency converter: OUT is a square wave whose
# frequency is proportional to the light on the selected photodiode group.
#   S2 S3: L L red, L H blue, H L clear (no filter), H H green   (datasheet Figure 5)
#   S0 S1: L L power down, L H 2 %, H L 20 %, H H 100 % of the full-scale frequency
#          (full scale typ. 12 kHz / 120 kHz / 600 kHz)
#   OE: active low output enable (high = OUT high-impedance)
# Inputs: VIH >= 2 V, so 3.3 V GPIOs drive them at any VDD. OUT swings to VDD, so power the
# module from 3.3 V when OUT goes to a 3.3 V GPIO. The divided (2 %/20 %) outputs are 50 % duty
# square waves; use 2 % (or 20 %) so a MicroPython interrupt can count every edge.
from machine import Pin
import time

RED, BLUE, CLEAR, GREEN = 0, 1, 2, 3          # value = S2*2 + S3
_SCALE = {0: (0, 0), 2: (0, 1), 20: (1, 0), 100: (1, 1)}


class TCS3200:
    def __init__(self, s0, s1, s2, s3, out, oe=None, scaling=2):
        self.s0 = Pin(s0, Pin.OUT)
        self.s1 = Pin(s1, Pin.OUT)
        self.s2 = Pin(s2, Pin.OUT)
        self.s3 = Pin(s3, Pin.OUT)
        self.oe = Pin(oe, Pin.OUT, value=0) if oe is not None else None  # OE low = output on
        self.out = Pin(out, Pin.IN)
        self._n = 0
        self.scaling(scaling)
        self.out.irq(trigger=Pin.IRQ_RISING, handler=self._edge)

    def _edge(self, p):
        self._n += 1

    def scaling(self, pct):
        """Output frequency scaling: 0 (power down), 2, 20 or 100 (%)."""
        a, b = _SCALE[pct]
        self.s0.value(a)
        self.s1.value(b)
        self.pct = pct

    def enable(self, on=True):
        if self.oe is not None:
            self.oe.value(0 if on else 1)

    def hz(self, colour, window_ms=100):
        """Select a photodiode group (RED/BLUE/CLEAR/GREEN) and return OUT's frequency in Hz,
        counted over window_ms."""
        self.s2.value(colour >> 1)
        self.s3.value(colour & 1)
        # The new period starts one output period (+1 us) after a select change; at the
        # 2 % scale's lowest useful rates a few ms is enough to settle.
        time.sleep_ms(5)
        n0 = self._n
        t0 = time.ticks_us()
        time.sleep_ms(window_ms)
        n = self._n - n0
        dt = time.ticks_diff(time.ticks_us(), t0)
        return n * 1000000 / dt

    def rgbc(self, window_ms=100):
        """(red, green, blue, clear) frequencies in Hz."""
        return (self.hz(RED, window_ms), self.hz(GREEN, window_ms),
                self.hz(BLUE, window_ms), self.hz(CLEAR, window_ms))

# TCS3200 colour sensor module (TCS3200)

## Overview
The **TCS3200** (ams, formerly TAOS; the older TCS230 is pin-compatible) has an 8 × 8 photodiode array: 16 photodiodes each with red, green and blue filters and 16 clear ones. A current-to-frequency converter turns the light on the selected group into a **square wave on OUT** whose frequency is proportional to irradiance. Hobbyists buy the square **28.4 × 28.4 mm TCS3200 / TCS230 colour recognition module** with four white LEDs around the chip and two 4-pin headers.

## Pinout (generic module, two headers on opposite edges)
| Header | Pin | Function |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | S0 | Output frequency scaling select |
| 1 | S1 | Output frequency scaling select |
| 1 | OE | Output enable, active low (high = OUT high-impedance) |
| 1 | GND | Ground |
| 2 | VCC | Supply 2.7–5.5 V (also lights the white LEDs) |
| 2 | OUT | Frequency output (push-pull, swings to VCC) |
| 2 | S2 | Photodiode (colour) select |
| 2 | S3 | Photodiode (colour) select |

The headers are on two edges, so the module is wired with jumper leads.

## Electrical limits
- Supply 2.7–5.5 V (abs. max 6 V). Chip 1.4 mA typ, 2 mA max; the four white LEDs draw more.
- Inputs: VIH ≥ 2 V, VIL ≤ 0.8 V at any VDD, so 3.3 V GPIOs drive them even at 5 V.
- OUT: VOH ≈ VDD (4–4.5 V at 5 V). **Power the module from 3.3 V** when OUT goes to an ESP32/Pico/Pi GPIO.
- Full-scale frequency: 600 kHz (100 %), 120 kHz (20 %), 12 kHz (2 %).

## Interface details
| S0 | S1 | Scaling | | S2 | S3 | Photodiodes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| L | L | Power down | | L | L | Red |
| L | H | 2 % | | L | H | Blue |
| H | L | 20 % | | H | L | Clear |
| H | H | 100 % | | H | H | Green |

- Frequency ∝ light: count rising edges on OUT for a fixed window (or time a period).
- The 2 % and 20 % outputs are 50 % duty square waves; 100 % is a fixed-width pulse train. Use **2 %** with MicroPython interrupt counting (up to 12 kHz).
- A change on S0–S3/OE takes effect after one new output period + 1 µs.
- Inputs must never float: drive OE low (or tie it to GND).

## Wiring
- ESP32: VCC → 3V3, GND → GND, S0 → GPIO25, S1 → GPIO26, S2 → GPIO27, S3 → GPIO14, OE → GPIO13 (or GND), OUT → GPIO34.
- Pico: VCC → 3V3(OUT), GND → GND, S0 → GP2, S1 → GP3, S2 → GP4, S3 → GP5, OE → GP6 (or GND), OUT → GP7.
- Raspberry Pi 4: VCC → pin 1 (3.3 V), GND → pin 6, S0–S3 → GPIO5/6/13/19, OE → GND, OUT → GPIO26.

## Using the driver
```python
from tcs3200 import TCS3200
cs = TCS3200(s0=25, s1=26, s2=27, s3=14, out=34, oe=13, scaling=2)
r, g, b, c = cs.rgbc(100)
print('R=%d G=%d B=%d C=%d' % (r, g, b, c))
```

## Gotchas
- Readings are raw frequencies, not RGB: calibrate against a black and a white card and map each channel between them.
- Ambient light and IR leak in: shield the sensor and keep a fixed distance (1–2 cm) to the target.
- Powered from 5 V, OUT reaches ~4.5 V and needs a divider into a 3.3 V GPIO; 3.3 V supply avoids that.
- S0 = S1 = L is power-down: OUT goes high-impedance and no pulses arrive.

example.code:
from tcs3200 import TCS3200, RED, GREEN, BLUE, CLEAR
import time

cs = TCS3200(s0={S0}, s1={S1}, s2={S2}, s3={S3}, out={OUT}, oe={OE}, scaling=2)  # 2 %: full scale 12 kHz
while True:
    r = round(cs.hz(RED), -2)
    g = round(cs.hz(GREEN), -2)
    b = round(cs.hz(BLUE), -2)
    c = round(cs.hz(CLEAR), -2)
    print('R=%d G=%d B=%d C=%d' % (r, g, b, c))
    time.sleep_ms(200)
